metadata.title: Mst. NASEEM MAI vs MASROOR ASHIQ KHAWAJA and another

full_text:
2010 Y L R 1945

[Lahore]

Before Hafiz Abdul Rehman Ansari, J

Mst. NASEEM
MAI---Petitioner

Versus

MASROOR ASHIQ
KHAWAJA and another---Respondents

Writ Petition No.
1574 of 2010, decided on 25th February, 2010.

West Pakistan Family Courts Act (XXXV of 1964)---

----S. 5 & Sched. ---Constitution of Pakistan
(1973), Art.199---Constitutional petition---Suit for dissolution of
marriage--Pending suit for dissolution of marriage filed by the petitioner
against the respondent, petitioner had sought direction to the Judge Family
Court to decide her suit in her favour---Validity---High Court could not issue
such direction or interfere in the cases pending before the lower
courts---Direction sought for from the High Court was highly unreasonable,
which was not permissible in any way under the law---Case of the petitioner
before the Judge Family Court could not be preferred against other cases, even
if petitioner was seeking direction for earlier disposal of her case.

Ch. Muhammad Iftikhar
Ahmad Joyia for Petitioner.

ORDER

HAFIZ ABDUL
REHMAN ANSARI, J.---Through this
constitutional petition, petitioner has sought direction to learned Judge
Family Court, D.G. Khan to dispose her suit for dissolution of marriage pending
before him in her favour.

2. The contents of
the writ petition revealed that there is serious dispute between the spouses.
The husband is harassing and humiliating the petitioner on one pretext or the
other and through registration of false cases against her.

3. Petitioner has
filed suit for dissolution of marriage on 9-2-2010 which is pending before the
learned Judge Family Court, D.G. Khan. Petitioner has sought direction to the
Judge Family Court to decide her suit in her favour. It is very strange that
through this writ petition interference and intercession is sought in the case
pending before the learned Judge Family Court for which this Court has no
authority to interfere in the cases pending before the learned Lower Courts.
Such prayer amounts to contempt of this Court. This Court cannot think of to
issue such direction or interference in the cases pending before the lower
Courts. The direction sought for from this Court is highly unreasonable which
is not permissible in any way under the law. The prayer made in writ petition
is reproduced as under:

"Under the above mentioned facts and circumstances, it is most
humbly prayed that this petition of the petitioner may very graciously be
accepted and necessary directions may kindly be issued to the learned Judge
Family Court, Dera Ghazi Khan, to dispose of the suit for dissolution of
marriage pending in his Court in favour of the petitioner, so that the
petitioner could take a sigh of relief and spend her life & liberty
according to her will and wishes."

The case of the
petitioner before the Judge Family Court cannot be preferred against other
cases even if petitioner is seeking direction for early disposal of her case.

4. With the above
observations, this writ petition is disposed of.

H.B.T./N-47/L Petition
dismissed.
